answer: Like a crystal lattice, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade. One real agent builds one reputation, but a sybil attacker must fund a whole dune of fake identities, each stake at risk of being slashed. Honest work slowly grows the stake, like a willow putting down roots, while detected fraud burns the deposit. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand stakes, so the attack becomes more expensive than any profit it could steal.
